text:
The Anaheim Ducks are winless in four (0-4-0), and this one slipped away early. The New York Islanders scored three times in the first period, twice in the opening 17 minutes, and then spent the rest of the night protecting a lead the Ducks could only trim. Alex Killorn's goal at 17:20 of the third made it 3-2, but it came too late to matter. Simon Holmstrom, who tipped in a power-play goal in the final minute and a half of the first, was named the game's first star.

The scoreboard understates how lopsided the play was. NYI took 77 shot attempts to ANA's 49, and in expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances, not just their number) the gap was 5.04 to 1.99. The first period was the widest, at 2.40 to 0.75. Another model, which replays every shot thousands of times, says the Islanders deserved to win 89 percent of the time. Lukas Dostal is the reason the margin was only one goal at the end. He saved 2.04 goals more than the chances he faced would typically allow, stopping 22 of 25 shots, while Ilya Sorokin stopped 15 of 17 behind a much quieter night for his defense.

Leo Carlsson had two assists for the Ducks, setting up both Frank Vatrano's goal late in the first and Killorn's late push. Anaheim finished 0 for 2 on the power play, while New York converted once in four chances. The loss leaves the Ducks winless in four. The facts don't include a streak or record for the Islanders, so there is nothing more to say about where this leaves them.
